Subject: Redwood private deploy — kickoff & peering questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are green-lit to proceed with a private deployment for the next phase. Before we lock dates, our infra team asked for a concise plan that covers VPC peering topology, private endpoints for the Redwood control plane, and what the on‑prem package needs for our edge racks. Can you share a proposed onboarding cadence and a baseline network requirements sheet we can hand to our SREs?

Key constraints on our side: single CIDR per VPC (10.40.0.0/16), strict outbound proxy through our corporate NAT, and HSM keys are managed by our security team (we use AWS KMS with an external HSM for keys-of-keys).

Also looping in procurement for contract cadence.

Appreciate a short checklist we can review with the network owners.

—Jared
Director, Platform Engineering
Medisync Inc.

Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — kickoff & peering questions

Jared — thanks for the context and the CIDR heads-up. We've prepared an onboarding cadence and a compact network checklist; attaching the baseline packet (redwood_onprem-deploy-checklist.pdf) and a draft network requirements worksheet (medisync-network-requirements.xlsx).

High-level proposal (short):
- Week 0: Security & contract signoff (DocuSign) + credentials exchange (KMS, account IDs).
- Week 1: Network review + VPC peering test (non-prod) — establish peering, route tables, and test ping/flows.
- Week 2: Private endpoint provisioning & TLS key exchange; edge appliance staging.
- Week 3: Staging traffic, KV cache warm, performance smoke tests.
- Week 4: Cutover window and rollback runbook.

Network notes for your SREs (summary):
- We support direct VPC peering or Transit Gateway. For a single CIDR on your side we recommend Transit Gateway only if you plan multiple AWS accounts; otherwise a single peering with route propagation is fine.
- Required outbound rules: allow egress to Redwood control plane on TCP 443 (TLS), and to our metrics/ingest endpoints on port 9001.
- If you enforce an explicit outbound proxy, provide proxy host/ports and a short-lived allowlist token; appliance will honor proxy envs.
- For HSM/KMS: we can integrate with your AWS KMS key material; our on‑prem agent supports local HSM unlocking via PKCS#11 if needed — we'll need the KMS key ARN and a contact in security for the HSM attestation flow.

Can we schedule a 60min technical review with your SREs on Wednesday (2026-09-02) 10:00 PT? I included a drive link with the packet. If that slot works we’ll include our networking lead (Markus) and implementation owner (Camila).

Thanks — laura
Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Jared / team — quick follow from our infra side with implementation specifics for your SREs (attached worksheet has the same rows):

1) CIDR & routing
   - We will not NAT your private CIDR; peering relies on explicit route table entries on both sides. Please confirm the exact subnets you want bound for peering (we suggest 10.40.8.0/24 for the peering endpoints).
2) BGP / Transit requirements
   - If you require dynamic routing we support TGW with BGP sessions to your appliances; otherwise static routes are easier and lower ops for single-account setups.
3) Private endpoint DNS
   - We recommend creating private hosted zones to resolve control-plane endpoints; we'll hand over a stub domain (redwood-control.internal.medisync) and require the VPC to allow conditional forwarders if you resolve it in-house.
4) Firewall / proxy
   - Outbound: TCP 443 to control-plane IPs, 9001 for metrics; Inbound: SSH only from our jump host for initial debugging (we'll request key-based access and rotate after onboarding).
5) Edge appliance needs
   - The appliance package needs 2 NICs, 16GB RAM, 4 cores minimum for staging; a 10G uplink preferred. The appliance will try to fetch an auth bundle at boot from our control-plane URL — ensure your proxy allows that fetch.

Attachments: medicsync-network-requirements.xlsx (row-level rules), edge-appliance-ops-guide.zip (appliance install artifacts).

If the 9/2 slot works we will prepare a live diagram and a preflight checklist so we can hit staging in Week 2.

—Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
